content: As dicsussed today, we can implement an AI assessment of PRs along a set of rubrics, like Tau Ceti does. This results in e.g. https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1206#issuecomment-6344001192 (on one of my own PRs). Please take a look. I can proceed to moving towards a PR.

The PR is at https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1934. This was work by Claude and I have not reviewed it in detail, but will do that later today time-permitting. It would need a repository action to add the label.

The new rubric over what is copied over from Tau Ceti (with suitable changes, including removal of aggressively adversarial role) is the physical relevance rubric, .agents/skills/ai-assessment/rubrics/physical-relevance.md, https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1934/changes#diff-f452145c7b1d74da22cabfebdffdf71ac914c6ab3e28e85397892b537b22f742. It asks (top line): "is the content physics, and is it mainstream physics?"

See ‎.agents/skills/ai-assessment/rubrics/NOTICE.md, https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1934/changes#diff-d009b9e65755c5f8214d2a73ed6b834b6810ba0671d2a801012be1c9957e1afe, for a summary of what was changed relative to Tau Ceti's rubrics.
How does this actually work in practice? How would I run it locally, and can I run it so that it does not post to the PR?

I think we should make:

This assessment makes no decisions and is intended to improve your PR where possible. Scores are from 0 to 5 per rubric; humans make every decision about this PR.

stronger:

This assessment is provided as a guide on how to make your PR as good as possible. However, the final review decision rests with humans, who may contradict or go against this assessment; their decision takes priority.

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

How does this actually work in practice? How would I run it locally, and can I run it so that it does not post to the PR?

From what I see in the SKILL.md it is by default something that a human must approve before posting.

## Ground rules

- **The human posts.** Communication with reviewers is conducted by humans (`AI-POLICY.md`
  §3.1). Never post a comment, edit a comment, or change a label without showing the user
  exactly what will be posted and getting their explicit confirmation, for each PR.

And as it is a skill, you should be able to just load it into your agent (or ask it to do it for you) and then invoke it with /ai-assessment, unless you decide to name it something else.

Yes, you'd use the /ai-assessment skill and you can add arguments to pick a specific PR or process any with the tag. It won't post by default (but that's a skill prompt language, not a hard block in code).

Maybe something like AI Notes would be better? Just tested this out locally and it looks great.

I wonder though if we could somehow make the rubrics (or the what to look at for part) readable by humans as well (maybe keep them somewhere in the ./docs).

Certainly can store in docs/. I have not looked at how they would make it onto the website from there (I assume that's where docs/ goes), or if that changes the format they should follow (e.g. md headers).
By default the docs don't go onto the website, and don't need a special md header from that point of view.
I've addressed these comments in https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1934 (which now doesn't conflict with master).
My other thought here was that maybe we could intergrate the rubric with the Tips that @Nathaneal Sajan has put together
That's a good suggestion, I have requested reviews for the tips PR from other maintainers so we can get some more heads on this. After that's merged we could work these together
Yeah, maybe we could have 'tips' for different areas, and the ai-assessement or ai-notes or similar measures alignment to those tips.
